author.text: Agentic implementation of #2129 Feature Request: Allow generation of Formatter for a type in a referenced assembly

verdict.classifier1: 3 changed project files (.csproj) are on the team's risky list.
verdict.reason: Two parts of the request have no proof yet.
blockers: No proof yet: the save-and-load code is made inside the project that uses the type.
No proof yet: a marked class with no body is accepted.

reviewSummary: The working case was not run by any unit test. There are also a few smaller bugs and some wrong docs.

findings.title: The working case was never tested
findings.detail: All 6 new unit tests that ran end with an error on purpose. None of them reaches the code that makes the output. So the main promise of the feature is unproven.

findings.title: One kind of type gets generated code that does not build
findings.detail: Some types run extra steps before saving and after loading. If the type sets those up in one specific way, the generated code calls a method that does not exist. The build then fails.

findings.title: The new code ignores a project setting
findings.detail: A project can ask for all data to be saved in map form. The new code ignores that. So one type is saved as a list while the rest are saved as maps.

findings.title: Generated code can vanish without a warning
findings.detail: If two pieces of generated code cover the same type, only the first one is kept. The user is not told.

findings.title: The README lists too few warnings
findings.detail: The README says the feature uses warnings MsgPack019 to MsgPack022. The code also raises MsgPack004, MsgPack005 and MsgPack007.

findings.title: A rule in the docs is not checked
findings.detail: The docs say outer classes must be marked partial. The code does not check this. The user gets a confusing compiler error, not the promised warning.

questions.question: Does a type from another project get working generated code?
questions.help: Run the unit tests that save and load such a type. They already exist.

questions.question: Is the short form with no class body accepted?
questions.help: A unit test that uses the short form.

questions.question: Is this the design the maintainers want? None of the three ideas in the request was built.
Is the default way of saving such a type the right one?
questions.help: The maintainers decide. Then a unit test locks it in.

questions.question: Does the app find and use the generated code?
questions.help: Run the unit test for this.

questions.question: Must the output stay the same for projects that do not use the feature?
questions.help: The maintainers confirm. The existing unit tests then check it.

agent.context: feature request #2129 and the 28 files this PR changes

chat.keys: approach attribute collector chose design marker
chat.a: The request asks for exactly this: mark a class and get the code made for you. The type itself cannot carry MessagePack marks, because its project cannot use MessagePack. So I read the type as it is. I added `SurrogateType` for when you want to pick the keys yourself.

chat.q: What were you least sure about?
chat.a: The project files. I added one project and edited two others. Your team treats those files as risky. I also did not handle map mode.
The unit tests that ran only cover the 4 new warnings. The working case, where code is really generated, was not run.

1.summary: Adds a new marker, `[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter]`. With it, a project can generate save-and-load code for a type that lives in another project. The unit tests that ran only cover the error cases. The normal, working case was not run.

sections.title: Why
sections.text: Project A cannot use MessagePack. So Project B needs to make the save-and-load code for Project A's type.

sections.title: Before → after
sections.text: Before: no way to do this. After: mark a class with `[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter]` and the code is made for you.

sections.title: Must preserve
sections.text: Projects that do not use the new marker must get the same output as before.

sections.title: Approach
sections.text: A new marker, new code that finds the marked classes, 4 new warnings (`MsgPack019` to `MsgPack022`), and edits to the code templates.

sections.title: Checks run
sections.text: Unit tests (`dotnet test`, a saved run on one machine, not the automatic server run): 173 of 173 pass. The 6 new unit tests that ran all stop before any code is generated.

sections.title: Open gaps
sections.text: No unit test that ran covers the working case. Also, 3 project files (`.csproj`) changed. The team treats those as risky.

sections.title: Rollback
sections.text: Undo the commit. Do it before a release, because users can see the new marker.
